title: Blueprint: Bluecurrent Shipping VPC/on-prem Rollout — Infrastructure Q&A & Upgrade Matrix
body:
Purpose / scope:
This is a working blueprint for the Bluecurrent Shipping private deployment (VPC + on-prem acceleration nodes). Focus: sizing guidance, Terraform module mapping, upgrade/rollback matrix, and a pragmatic cutover checklist. Intended audience: SEs, infra eng, customer SRE, and delivery PM.

Customer context (short):
- Bluecurrent Shipping: logistics + fleet telematics; strict data residency in EU + additional latency sensitivity for manifest generation (95th p90 < 120ms).
- Expected steady-state: 80 TPS inference requests at peak business hours for reranking and manifest generation. Token profile: median 64 tokens, p95 320 tokens.
- Security: customer uses Azure VNet + on-prem GPU rack behind transit gateway. KMS is Azure Key Vault (HSM-backed).

High-level goals / constraints:
- Keep tail latency under 200ms for <= 3 token responses and under 800ms p95 for 320-token requests (best-effort for long sequences).
- Single-account tenancy; data never leaves customer VPC for private component. Hosted control plane with customer-managed egress rules.
- Minimal downtime during upgrade windows; allow rolling kernel and driver updates with automatic fallback to hosted variants.

Assumptions (call out):
- We'll use model variants quantized to int8 for production path (acceptable per Bluecurrent QA).
- Average concurrency per GPU: 8 concurrent streams for A100-80GB, 10 for H100-80GB (scheduling safety factor 0.7).
- Customer will procure 3x H100-80GB nodes for initial pool (one hot spare).
- NVMe local storage for model cache: 1.5TB per node.
- Networking: 25 Gbps interconnect per node, BGP routed to customer transit gateway.

Sizing summary (initial recommendation):
- Serving pool: 3 H100-80GB nodes, each with 80GB GPU, 256GB host RAM, 24 vCPUs. Rationale: supports the 80 TPS peak with headroom for autoscaling bursts to 5x baseline if needed.
- Control/management plane: 2 m5a.4xlarge-equivalent controllers in customer VPC to host agent/control-plane connector (HA pair).
- Storage: 1x 10TB network file store for artifacts + model artifacts stored in customer S3-compatible (minio/on-prem).
- Observability: 5 day raw token retention onsite, metrics aggregated to hosted console (obfuscated tokens).

Terraform module mapping / notes (practical bits):
- Use terraform-modules/vpc/bluecurrent-az-vnet (pin to v1.3.2) instead of the generic vpc module due to custom peering logic.
- Create new module wrapper private-deploy/bluecurrent-agent with parameters: customer_id, kv_endpoint, allowed_subnets. Keep it tiny — avoid heavy logic in module to ease future upgrades.
- Module variables to expose: gpu_node_type (string), node_count_min, node_count_max, kms_key_alias, allowed_cidrs, monitoring_endpoint.
- State: use remote backend with locking (azurerm/terraform cloud) — ensure state policy disallows public access.
- Upgrade flag in modules: enable_runtime_quantization (default false) — flip in staged rollouts.
- Critical: add a terraform-built sentinel resource that creates a DNS CNAME for agent-to-control-plane with TTL 30s to enable quick rollback to alternate control endpoints.

Compatibility & upgrade matrix (what to test and how):
- Driver/OS: GPU driver must match kern-driver mapping v525.x for H100. We will maintain images: h100-ubuntu-22.04-gdr-525 (immutable image tag).
- Runtime: Redwood runtime v2.7.x supports int8 quantization paths; earlier v2.6.x lacks some kernel selection optimizations — do not upgrade runtime in same window as driver.
- Quantization: validate output quality with an automated eval set (customer-provided) across canary subset before enabling int8 global rollout.

Phased rollout plan (4 phases):
1) Infra provisioning (lab staging): provision 1 node + control pair, smoke test network, KMS connectivity.
2) Canary (on-prem): add second node; deploy runtime v2.7.0, run small canary traffic 5 TPS, run evals, compare logits/regression.
3) Gradual scale: scale to 3 nodes, enable autoscaler (min=2 max=6), enable local NVMe cache warming, run 72h soak.
4) Live cutover: redirect 25% traffic -> private pool for 24h -> 50% for 12h -> 100% after 48h if no regression.

Rollback criteria: any of the following triggers immediate rollback to hosted fallback model or older runtime image:
- >=5% increase in token cost or 10% increase in median latency over baseline
- Functional regressions detected by eval suite (classification accuracy drop >1.5% absolute for critical prompts)
- Node-level OOM or repeated OOM kills >2 within 1 hour

Cutover checklist (short actionable items):
- Pre-cutover (T-7d): finalize TF vars, get customer approval for KMS IAM binding, CI PR for modules merged.
- T-2d: provision nodes, validate BGP + MTU + route tables, verify KMS access under customer account.
- T-2h: warm model cache (night-run), run full eval set, snapshot metrics baseline.
- Cutover window: perform DNS switch (TTL 30s), watch metrics, keep rollback window open for 4h.
- Post-cutover (T+24h): run 48h soak, archive logs to S3, schedule debrief.

Operational gotchas & notes to self: 
- Azure private endpoints drop ICMP; ensure our health checks use TCP/HTTP probes only.
- Drift detection: enable terraform plan guardrails in PR pipelines, add automation to create drift alerts to #private-deploy-bluecurrent.
- Autoscaler grief: customer network ACLs occasionally block scale-up. Add preflight check that attempts to open ephemeral ports 20000-20010.

Open questions (owner / target date):
- Q1: Does Bluecurrent insist on air-gapped model refreshes (manual import) or is VPN-based S3 replication acceptable? (Owner: Marcus Flynn, due: 2025-02-21)
- Q2: Any regulatory requirement to run inference on FIPS-certified crypto modules (HSM)? If yes, we need extra KMS adapter. (Owner: Priya Desai, due: 2025-02-18)
- Q3: Acceptable RTO for control-plane failover? If < 5min need hot-hot controllers. (Owner: Evelyn Park, due: 2025-02-20)

Action items / next steps:
- Marcus: finalize TF wrapper PR and pin modules (PR #214 referenced).
- Priya: validate KMS IAM flow with Bluecurrent security and produce short runbook for HSM fallback.
- Liam: create eval suite (50 prompts) and add to CI gating.
- Evelyn: schedule cutover dry-run with customer SRE (target week of 2025-03-03).

Quick notes (scratch):
- Consider offering an initial hybrid config where reranking uses private pool and long-LLM generation keeps using hosted to minimize cost.
- Add a manual step to disable quantization before a kernel upgrade to reduce surface area.

Draft history / provenance:
- Created by Evelyn Park 2025-02-10 after first scoping call (Bluecurrent).
- Iterated with SEs Marcus and Priya 2025-02-12 and 2025-02-15.
- Updated sizing after customer inventory (2025-02-17).

---
Notes end. This remains a working draft; expect changes after security deep-dive and procurement confirmation.
